record.question: Which of the following is the most effective strategy to minimize dispensing errors in a busy high patient load pharmacy setting?
options: Encouraging faster dispensing to reduce patient waiting time
Storing look-alike/sound-alike (LASA) drugs together for convenience
Allowing verbal prescriptions to be filled immediately without documentation
Using a double-check system involving two pharmacists for high-risk prescriptions
record.explanation: Answer D: Using a double-check system involving two pharmacists for high-risk prescriptions. A second independent check for high-risk prescriptions can catch selection, dose, and calculation errors in a busy pharmacy. Source/context note: Independent double checks should be targeted to high-risk processes and designed to avoid ineffective routine checking. Reference: https://www.ismp.org/recommendations/tall-man-letters. Verified worked solution, unofficial. Original printed wording and option order reviewed; no matching examiner key is asserted.
